title: How would you estimate how many full-time wedding photographers the UK needs?
description: A step-by-step estimate for "How many full-time wedding photographers does the UK need?" with the approach, the maths and a sanity check.
hook: The UK needs about 10,000 full-time wedding photographers: roughly 250,000 weddings a year that hire a professional, divided by about 25 weddings one photographer can shoot and edit in a year. The interesting judgement is that capacity: weddings cluster on summer weekends, and each one brings days of editing. Try your own estimate before you read on.
body:
The question

How many full-time wedding photographers does the UK need?

This is a short, two-step estimate: demand divided by capacity. It rewards candidates who think about how the work is actually done, because a wedding photographer's year is shaped by seasons, Saturdays and editing time.

Clarify before you calculate

  • Full-time equivalents or people? The question says full-time, so size full-time equivalents (FTEs). Many real photographers shoot weddings part time alongside other work.
  • One photographer per wedding? Start with one, then adjust for second shooters.
  • Which weddings? All UK marriages and civil partnerships where the couple hires a professional.

Rough guess: "Low tens of thousands at most. It is a niche trade."

Step by step

1. Weddings per year

There are roughly 280,000 weddings a year across the UK. This one is worth knowing roughly: the ONS recorded about 247,000 marriages in England and Wales in 2022, National Records of Scotland about 30,000 in 2022, and NISRA about 7,500 in Northern Ireland in 2023. That is about 284,000 in total.

2. Weddings that book a professional

Assume 9 in 10. Small register-office ceremonies often rely on a friend with a camera. 280,000 × 90% = 252,000, so about 250,000 bookings.

3. Weddings one photographer can do a year

Build it from the calendar. The main season runs from about April to October, roughly 30 weeks. A photographer can shoot about one wedding a week in season, because each wedding takes a full day on site plus several days of editing, meetings and admin. Allow for some weekends off and a few winter weddings, and a full-time wedding photographer does about 25 weddings a year.

4. Divide

250,000 ÷ 25 = 10,000 full-time wedding photographers.

Sanity check from a second angle

Check that 10,000 photographers can cover the busiest day of the year. The ONS reports that the most popular date in 2022 was Saturday 30 July, with 3,608 weddings in England and Wales. Scaling to the UK (× 284 ÷ 247) and to the 90% who book a professional gives about 3,700 photographers needed at once. That is well within a pool of 10,000. So peak days do not bind; the annual limit comes from editing time, not from the number of Saturdays.

A second check: the ONS also reports that 43.6% of 2022 marriages took place on a Saturday. Applied to 250,000 bookings, that is about 109,000 Saturday weddings, or about 2,100 on an average Saturday. Spread across 10,000 photographers, each works only some Saturdays, which fits the picture of a seasonal trade.

Source: ONS: Marriages in England and Wales, 2021 and 2022.

Which assumption matters most

Weddings per photographer. At 20 a year, the answer becomes 250,000 ÷ 20 = 12,500. At 30 a year, it is about 8,300. Second shooters matter too: if 30% of couples book a second photographer, assignments rise to 250,000 × 1.3 = 325,000, and the need rises to 325,000 ÷ 25 = 13,000 FTEs.

What a strong answer sounds like

"There are roughly 280,000 UK weddings a year, and I'll assume 90% book a professional, so about 250,000 jobs. A full-time photographer can do about one a week across a 30-week season, minus some weekends off, so around 25 a year once editing is included. That's about 10,000 full-time photographers, or 13,000 if 30% of couples hire a second shooter. The real number of people will be higher, because many do weddings part time."

A weak answer assumes a photographer works every Saturday of the year (52 weddings), which ignores both seasonality and the editing that follows each shoot, and halves the answer.

Common mistakes

  • Capacity from shooting days alone. The shoot is one day. Editing, client meetings and travel take several more.
  • Treating weddings as evenly spread. Demand is concentrated in summer, so check whether peak days constrain supply.
  • Answering with headcount. The demand-and-capacity method gives FTEs. Convert only if the interviewer asks for people.

Practice

1. Half of all bookings go to part-timers who average 8 weddings a year; the rest go to full-timers doing 25. How many people photograph UK weddings?

Show the answer

Full-timers: 125,000 ÷ 25 = 5,000. Part-timers: 125,000 ÷ 8 = about 15,600. Total about 20,600 people, roughly double the FTE number.

2. What do UK couples spend on wedding photography each year?

Show the answer

250,000 bookings × an average fee of $2,500 = about $625M a year.

Where to practise next

The same demand-over-capacity method answers how many hairdressers work in London and how many dentists the UK needs. For the overall method, read how to answer a market sizing question step by step, then try timed reps in the market sizing drill.
